Intense Survival Game with Tons of Depth

"SCUM" is a hardcore survival game that’s perfect if you love a challenge. You start off as a prisoner on a huge island and have to manage everything from your metabolism to your gear while dealing with other players and zombies. The detail is crazy, and the realism makes every decision count.

The world is massive and full of things to discover, and the character customization is top-notch. It can be tough at first, but once you get into it, it’s incredibly rewarding. If you’re into survival games, "SCUM" is definitely worth a try!

I got this game because I couldn't play Dead Matter due to their website never loading.

Other than the character creator crashes, i've only had good experiences with this game. Rented a server for 3 days to stress test it.
Most survival games in my experience run like crap.
I have a 2070 and 9600k.
This game runs awesome and i've been able to get playable performance after spawning over 100 zombies in the games largest city.

The games background character simulations are very complex but awesome if you take the time to learn how to take care of everything. It's very min-max.
My bullets hit their intended target.
Players and Zombies don't rubberband.
Character Awareness stat makes this the most balanced 1st and 3rd person survival game that currently exist to the best of my knowledge.
Parkour exist.
You don't need to spend 2 hours to find a gun. Maybe ammo in some cases if you don't take time to learn crafting.

If you find a good long-term pvp server you will have one hell of a time.

For me, the game really started going downhill after the most recent updates—essentially anything released after 0.7. I stayed supportive through each update, always hoping that some of the long-standing bugs and underlying issues would finally be addressed rather than continuing to prioritize cosmetic additions. Unfortunately, that hope turned out to be wishful thinking.

Whatever changed within the company after 0.7 fundamentally changed the direction of the game, and unfortunately, it has ruined the experience for me. I genuinely believe this game could be amazing under the right leadership and with the right priorities, but at this point, I don't see that happening.

As much as I wanted to continue supporting the game, I can't recommend purchasing it in its current state. There is a lot of potential here, but the current direction has made it very difficult to justify supporting the game.

SCUM is an enjoyable game. I like the fact there is a single-player mode to permit one to understand the mechanics of basic game play before jumping into an online server. I also appreciate the fact that one can have multiple characters where one may be for a "legit" experience and another that leverages the console to drop items to try out.

First and foremost, I used to play a lot up to .8. Once they broke basically all vehicles in the game and didn't prioritize a fast fix I wrote this game off.

That said, my game experience in SCUM, WAS at one time one of the more enjoyable survival games I've played.

Yes, it is early access and definitely, there are bugs / glitches, but the dev team is more focused on junk updates than actual core functionality optimization and bug fixes.

The graphics are truly some of the better I've seen and the environment with the last release has me constantly stopping play to just enjoy the sunset or afternoon storm rolling in. That gets lost pretty quick once you start feeling the bugs.

This game has been early access for YEARS AND YEARS.

Sons of the Forest in it's first early release had less bugs that this game. There are two week development cycles bringing real value to each update.

Honestly I can't remember the last time I saw something worth while get added in SCUM. Planes and Motorcycles then the game had a MAJOR MAJOR setback. I watch the updates but nothing has enticed me to return at this point.

That's really disappointing too, because I used to really enjoy this game.

I would also suggest moving away from just box lotting with a random outcome to a more visual representation of the loot. For example, if something was looted that it would look open. If there is a gun in the room, then it would be standing in its 3d model in the corner. If there is stuff in the box that it would be there with the camera zooming in. It would be nice to have something like a radar signal that would mark nearby looting objects. Overall, it will eliminate the feeling that you are grinding in repetitive action for nothing. There a lot of room to remove boredom and create more immerse looting system that would have excitement when you arrive in the new town and remove the feeling of "been there done that", at the end of the day this whole game build around looting and rooming around looking for loot, so that crucial part need to be solid and exciting! I've been playing this on and off again for a year with friends, always checking out new updates, and we've had nothing but fun with it. All of the negative reviews I've read so far are completely asinine. The dev team been working on this title non-stop, even through holidays, for a straight year to release continuous patches to both fix bugs and provide a slew of new content.

All the bitching about bugs in an Early Access title, I've experienced very few bugs in my playtime. All the whinging about hackers, I've not encountered a single instance of it across multiple servers. Not saying it isn't happening, but it seems greatly exaggerated.

This game, from day one, exceeded my expectations after years of disappointing experiences with projects such as DayZ and Miscreated that were going nowhere. The content, the mechanics that are constantly updated and lending a level of sophistication to the game make it really unique. Would really love to see more story options and player progression for longevity, but that is already being worked on as indicated by the new Journal option.

Either way, this game has been amazing, and extremely hilarious in a lot of ways, and will be in my Steam library indefinitely.

As of 10th August 2025, one of the biggest frustration for players is the issue that have not been fixed like rapidly despawning loot and bodies.

SCUM is one of the best survival games I’ve ever played, & I’ve played a lot.
From the moment you spawn in your orange jumpsuit with nothing but fists & fear, it throws you straight into chaos. Whether you're dodging puppets, scouring bunkers for loot, or trying not to starve while crafting makeshift gear, every moment feels intense & rewarding. The survival mechanics are incredibly detailed, from metabolism & vitamins to weather & clothing insulation. It adds depth without feeling overwhelming once you get the hang of it.

Base building is a blast, especially with friends. Want to live deep in the woods? Build a compound? Set traps for raiders? Go full wilderness goblin? You can. & the multiplayer aspect makes it even better, some of the funniest, wildest moments I’ve had in gaming have happened in SCUM.

It's not just about surviving, it's about thriving in your own chaotic, creative way. The devs continue to add content & polish, & it's clear this game has heart behind it. If you love survival games with depth, danger, & freedom, SCUM is 100% worth your time.
